Author’s note

A friend recently asked me for course recommendations, and similar questions have come up before, so I’ve rounded up what’s on offer. I’d also like to ask you: which corner of acoustics or audio do you work in? And if you had to take one course in your field, what would you want it to be? Let me know in the comments!

Of the courses listed below, I have taken two myself, edX’s Fundamentals of Communication Acoustics and Coursera’s Digital Signal Processing Specialization, and I thought both were very good. Suggestions and additions are welcome!

Free courses

  1. Coursera: Audio Signal Processing for Music Applications

    • Platform: Coursera

    • Institution: Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Barcelona, and Stanford University

    • What it covers: Audio signal processing with a focus on music: spectral analysis, audio effects (such as reverb and EQ), synthesis techniques and real-time processing in Python, including the Fourier transform and filter design. About 10 weeks at 4–6 hours a week.

    • Format: Free to audit, with an optional paid certificate (about US$49; check the website for current pricing). Self-paced, and a good introduction to signal processing for music.

    • Who it’s for: Music technology enthusiasts, signal processing beginners and audio engineers.

    • Link: https://www.coursera.org/learn/audio-signal-processing

  2. edX: Fundamentals of Digital Signal Processing

    • Platform: edX

    • Institution: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)

    • What it covers: The core concepts of digital signal processing (DSP), including discrete-time signals, the z-transform and filter design, with particular emphasis on audio and communications applications. About 6–8 weeks.

    • Format: Free to audit, with an optional paid verified certificate (about US$99). Self-paced, and well suited to learners with an engineering background.

    • Who it’s for: Engineering students and newcomers to audio signal processing.

    • Link: https://www.edx.org/learn/signal-processing/epfl-digital-signal-processing-1

  3. MIT OpenCourseWare: Signals and Systems

    • Platform: MIT OpenCourseWare

    • Institution: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)

    • What it covers: The foundations of signal processing, including continuous- and discrete-time systems, Fourier analysis and the Laplace transform, all applicable to audio processing and acoustics. Lecture notes, assignments and exams are provided.

    • Format: Completely free and self-paced; good for self-study or as a supplement.

    • Who it’s for: Engineering students and anyone interested in acoustics and audio processing.

    • Link: https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-007-signals-and-systems-spring-2011/

  4. Khan Academy: Signals and Systems (selected topics)

    • Platform: Khan Academy

    • What it covers: Introductory tutorials on signal processing, such as convolution, Fourier series and basic filtering, with some material touching on audio signal processing (for example, waveform analysis). The videos are short and to the point, ideal for getting started quickly.

    • Format: Completely free, beginner-friendly and concise.

    • Who it’s for: Signal processing beginners and newcomers to audio processing.

    • Link: https://www.khanacademy.org/science/electrical-engineering/ee-signals

  5. edX: Introduction to Audio and Music Engineering

    • Platform: edX

    • Institution: University of Rochester

    • What it covers: An introduction to audio engineering and music technology: the physics of sound, recording techniques, the basics of audio signal processing and the use of digital audio workstations (DAWs) in music production. Suited to beginners with an interest in audio engineering.

    • Format: Free to audit, with an optional paid certificate (about US$99). About 6 weeks at 3–5 hours a week.

    • Who it’s for: Audio engineers, music producers and beginners.

    • Link: https://www.edx.org/learn/audio-engineering/university-of-rochester-introduction-to-audio-and-music-engineering

  6. edX: Fundamentals of Communication Acoustics

    • Platform: edX

    • Institutions: Technical University of Munich (TUM), RWTH Aachen University, TU Berlin, TU Dresden and Chalmers University of Technology

    • What it covers: An engineering course on the fundamentals of communication acoustics, which studies how sound travels from a source through a channel to a receiver. Topics include speech acoustics, hearing acoustics, electroacoustics, the human auditory system and digital audio processing. The instructors are experts from leading German technical universities, among them Gerhard Müller and Michael Vorländer. About 6 weeks at 6–8 hours a week.

    • Format: Free to audit, with an optional paid certificate (about US$29). Assumes basic knowledge of signals and systems (linearity, time invariance, the Fourier transform). Afterward you can continue with the follow-up course, Applications in Communication Acoustics.

    • Who it’s for: Engineering students and practitioners in acoustics and audio processing.

    • Link: https://www.edx.org/learn/engineering/rwthtumx-fundamentals-of-communication-acoustics

Paid courses

  1. Coursera: Digital Signal Processing Specialization

    • Platform: Coursera

    • Institution: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)

    • What it covers: A four-course specialization covering DSP fundamentals, the Fourier transform, filter design and applications in audio and image processing, with Python-based labs. About 4 months at 5 hours a week.

    • Format: Paid subscription (about US$49 a month; check the website for current pricing), certificate included. Suited to more advanced learners.

    • Who it’s for: Engineering students and audio signal processing practitioners.

    • Link: https://www.coursera.org/specializations/digital-signal-processing

  2. Coursera: Fundamentals of Audio and Music Technology

    • Platform: Coursera

    • Institution: University of Michigan

    • What it covers: The basics of audio engineering, including microphones, loudspeakers, digital audio processing, mixing and mastering. It covers both the theory and the practice of audio signal flow and suits beginners in music production and audio technology. About 6 weeks at 4 hours a week.

    • Format: Paid (about US$49 a month; check the website), certificate included. Self-paced.

    • Who it’s for: Music producers and newcomers to audio technology.

    • Link: https://www.coursera.org/learn/audio-engineering

  3. Udemy: Digital Signal Processing with MATLAB (Codes Included)

    • What it covers: A hands-on DSP course covering signal analysis, filtering and speech signal processing, with practical MATLAB projects such as designing audio filters. About 7–10 hours.

    • Format: Paid (about US$10–100 depending on discounts), with lifetime access and a certificate of completion. Good for people who learn by doing.

    • Who it’s for: Engineering students and audio signal processing practitioners.

    • Link: https://www.udemy.com/course/digital-signal-processing-with-matlab/

  4. Udemy: Building Acoustics and Noise Control

    • What it covers: Acoustic design for buildings, covering outdoor acoustics, room acoustics, sound insulation, impact noise and sustainable design, with case studies, spreadsheet calculations and audio demonstrations. A good entry point into acoustic consulting.

    • Format: Paid (about US$10–50 depending on discounts), with lifetime access, a certificate of completion and the spreadsheets. Requires basic math.

    • Who it’s for: Engineering and architecture students and people working in the building industry.

    • Link: https://www.udemy.com/course/building-acoustics-and-noise-control/

  5. Udemy: Acoustics: Practical Indoor Sound Treatment

    • What it covers: Acoustic treatment for recording and professional spaces, dealing with echo, reverberation, background noise and uneven sound fields. It introduces a four-part approach (positioning, sealing, screening and damping) that can be applied to walls, windows, doors, ceilings and floors. It also covers post-production techniques and emphasizes budget-friendly solutions, starting from US$0. About 2.5 hours.

    • Format: Paid (about US$10–50), with lifetime access and a certificate of completion. Suited to content creators.

    • Who it’s for: Podcasters, recording engineers and home theater owners.

    • Link: https://www.udemy.com/course/practical-indoor-acoustics/

  6. Udemy: Principles of Acoustics for the Home Studio

    • What it covers: Acoustic treatment for home studios, rehearsal rooms and home theaters, covering how sound behaves indoors and outdoors, with an emphasis on simple, practical methods and no advanced math. About 2–3 hours.

    • Format: Paid (about US$10–50), with lifetime access and a certificate of completion.

    • Who it’s for: Musicians and audio enthusiasts.

    • Link: https://www.udemy.com/course/principles-of-acoustics-for-the-home-studio/

  7. Udemy: Acoustics 101: Speaker Design Basics and Enclosure Design

    • What it covers: How to design sealed and bass-reflex loudspeaker enclosures, covering the basics of sound waves, enclosure trade-offs (loudness, bass extension, linearity) and building your own DIY audio system, using free software such as WinISD and SketchUp.

    • Format: Paid (about US$10–50), with lifetime access, a certificate of completion and Excel spreadsheets.

    • Who it’s for: Audiophiles and DIY audio hobbyists.

    • Link: https://www.udemy.com/course/acoustics-101-speaker-design-basics-and-enclosure-design/

  8. Udemy: Learning Audiate from Scratch

    • What it covers: A complete guide to the Audiate audio editor, covering recording, editing, noise removal, inserting and deleting silence, waveform editing and audio enhancement, for podcasters, content creators and voice artists. About 2–3 hours.

    • Format: Paid (about US$10–50 depending on discounts), with lifetime access and a certificate of completion. Suited to beginners in audio post-production.

    • Who it’s for: Podcasters, content creators and voice artists.

    • Link: https://www.udemy.com/course/learningaudiate/

  9. Udemy: Audio Engineering: All About EQ

    • What it covers: How to use equalizers (EQ) in audio engineering, covering frequency balance, filter types, EQ in the mix and hands-on audio signal processing. Suited to music production and recording. About 2 hours.

    • Format: Paid (about US$10–50), with lifetime access and a certificate of completion.

    • Who it’s for: Audio engineers and music producers.

    • Link: https://www.udemy.com/course/audio-engineering-all-about-eq/
